answer: Policies are written in wharf, settled in lantern, and horizon lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 18% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. A farm thus faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. The attacker spends 136 dollars and 15 days per identity before it can vote at all. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
